This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.224/2017 dated 03.01.2018 on the file of the Prl. Senior Civil Judge & CJM, Chitradurga.
2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation for the death of minor daughter of the claimant who was six years old as on the date of the accident.

The Tribunal towards loss of dependency had granted an amount of Rs.5,60,000/-, towards medical expenses granted an amount of Rs.41,235/-,

sentences.text: 2 towards pain and agony granted an amount of Rs.20,000/-.
Altogether compensation of an amount of Rs.6,21,235/- which is rounded of to Rs.6,21,200/- was granted by the MACT.
3. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the amount that was arrived by the Tribunal is contrary to the settled law.

He submits that the Court below has observed that the earlier Judgment of Hon'ble NC: 2023:KHC:41973 Apex Court in the case of Kishangopal and another - Vs- Lala and others 1 has considered notional income at an amount of Rs.30,000/- and by applying multiplier 17 granted an amount of Rs.5,10,000/- under the head of loss of dependency and an amount of Rs.50,000/- under the conventional heads, towards loss of love and affection and funeral expenses i.e., (Rs.5,10,000/- + Rs.50,000/- =Rs.5,60,000/-).

entities.text: Kishangopal and another - Vs- Lala and others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Altogether compensation of an amount of Rs.5,60,000/- is granted under the said head.
4. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the court below without considering the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, had granted the compensation of an amount of Rs.6,21,235/-.
It is submitted that the compensation is unreasonable.
Learned counsel submits that the court below had granted interest at 9% which is exorbitant.
There is no representation on behalf of the respondents.

By referring the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal & another case referred supra, and another case of Kurvan Ansari @Kurvan Ali & another -Vs- Shyam Kishore Murmu & another2 and later in the case of Meenadevi -Vs- Luluchand Mehtho3, the court below had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.5,60,000/- towards of loss of dependency.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari @Kurvan Ali & another -Vs- Shyam Kishore Murmu & another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By applying the ratio referred supra, under the head of loss of dependency, they are entitled for an amount of Rs.4,50,000/-.
Towards other conventional heads this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/-.
In this case, an amount of Rs.41,235/- is spent towards medical expenses and this court finds no reasons to interfere.
Altogether the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.5,41,235/- at 6% interest.

The claimant is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Description of Items Compensation Awarded No.
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 4,50,000/-

2. Conventional heads Rs. 50,000/-
3. Medical Expenses Rs. 41,235/-
Total Rs. 5,41,235/-
7.
